items.note: Multi-armed Śiva Naṭeśa near the south mukhamaṇḍapa, an ūrdhvatāṇḍava image with drum-playing attendant.
Six images on the south-east tilaka: two Śakti images enclose four Śiva images.
Syncretic image of Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī and Sarasvatī (Vedamātās); Sarasvatī much venerated by the Paramāra royal family as goddess of learning.
Gāyatrī image combines knowledge (Veda, vitarka mudrā, akṣasūtra) and martial aspects; pāśa as snare of ignorance in Śaiva philosophy.
Seated Śiva images on the tilaka niches with jaṭāmukuṭa and ten arms; attributes listed.
Two types of Umā-Maheśvara image on the vedibandha khattikās: seated on a pedestal, or with mounts.
Hamsavatī, chief Śakti presiding over the ājñā cakra, placed on the tilaka corresponding to the forehead.
Bhairava worship became more tantric by medieval times (Harṣacarita); in Paramāra sculptures Bhairava appears with both dog and corpse.
Gaṇeśa in lalitāsana, four-armed, on the vedibandha khattikā below Naṭeśa.
Varuṇa on the north-west side with pāśa, standing on a crocodile.
Aparājitapṛcchā description of Varuṇa; the north-facing deity identified as Īśāna by his bull mount.
Twisted hip pose of the Naṭeśa also seen in a Paramāra Śiva from the Ambarnath temple (11th century CE), Maharashtra.
Vāyu with consort Śivā; image follows the Aparājitapṛcchā, Kāmikāgama and Viṣṇudharmottara descriptions.
Mahiṣāsuramardinī as the most popular manifestation of Śakti, formed from the anger of the gods.
Aparājitapṛcchā description of the goddess's weapons and Mahiṣa below.
Kāśyapa Śilpaśāstra and Ajitāgama descriptions of the goddess (breast-band, short skirt).
Multi-armed Mahiṣāsuramardinī near the north mukhamaṇḍapa seizing Mahiṣāsura's forelocks as in the Aparājitapṛcchā.
Following canonical injunctions, Mahiṣāsura arises from the severed neck, now in human form.
Possible Kubera image; positions of Kubera and Īśāna seem reversed, perhaps for symmetry of arrangement.
Dikpālas with elephant and bovine mounts placed in corresponding positions.
Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra description of Brahmā as quoted in translation for the Brahmā image.
Much mutilated multi-armed Cāmuṇḍā, emaciated, standing on a corpse.
Cāmuṇḍā's terrible form: kings and powerful lords were great devotees.
Paramāras of Vāgaḍa depicted Cāmuṇḍā in northern quarters; similar northern placement and scorpion at Udayeśvara.
North-east tilaka: four Śiva images between two Śakti images, with Cāmuṇḍā and Śiva.
Yogeśvarī with elephant in upper right hand and crescent on jaṭāmukuṭa, a Śaivite goddess.
Three-headed eight-armed Hariharārkapitāmaha facing east, central image Sūrya, face squarish in Paramāra idiom.
The image matches Ardhanarīśvara on the corresponding side, giving symmetry also seen in the dikpālas.
Ardhanarīśvara and Hara-Gaurī, Bhairava and Cāmuṇḍā placed on corresponding khattakas with balanced design.
Aparājitapṛcchā and Ajitāgama prescriptions for Īśāna and the diadems of the dikpālas.
Devatāmūrtiprakaraṇa places Vīreśvara amid the mātṛkās; six goddesses encircle Vīrabhadra, forming the aṣṭamātṛkās on the south latā.
Vīrabhadra image mutilated; prostrate Dakṣa Prajāpati shown per legend.
The central buttress of the garbhagṛha has the dikpālas, like the gūḍhamaṇḍapa.
Viṣṇu images are few since the temple has a strong Śaivite sculptural programme.
Vīrabhadra on the west latā surrounded by mātṛkās, forming the aṣṭamātṛkā group.
Śaivite Nandikeśvarī supplants Vaiṣṇava Vārāhī, a deliberate attempt to give an exclusive Śaivite character.
Kārttikeya on the west latā: six faces, twelve hands per canonical injunctions, peacock mount.
Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra description of Kārttikeya as quoted in translation.
Arrangement of Umā-Maheśvara, Gaṇeśa-Gaṇeśāṇī and Brahmā-Brahmāṇi on the khattikās between south latā and west latā.
Kaumārī, consort of Kumāra, three faces and four arms, stands in abhaṅga with fine chiselling.
Kumāra's tiara embellished with pearls and gems as described in the Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra.
Central buttress of the west-north section holds dikpālas according to the temple's iconographic programme.
Kubera on a vedibandha khattikā with treasure bag, citron and cup; Aparājitapṛcchā cited.
Attendants are the personified nidhis Padma and Śaṁkha.
Seated four-armed Sarasvatī on the fifth buttress vedibandha, defaced.
Cāmuṇḍā on the north latā with scorpion on belly, encircled by mātṛkās with Māheśvarī as the eighth.
Sculptural programme reflects Śaiva Siddhānta; Śakti dominates the left half of the temple.
Cāmuṇḍā and Mahiṣāsuramardinī on the north latā and north-east side; the three latās are encircled by aṣṭamātṛkās; eight devakulikās may have housed them, per Kāmikāgama.
Khattikās between north latā and north kapilī house three Umā-Maheśvara images and one Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
The only Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa image in the temple, tucked away in a shadowed khattikā.
Three-faced Brahmā on lotus pedestal below the north kapilī with consort Sāvitrī, mutilated.
Viṣṇudharmottara Mahāpurāṇa prescription for Brahmā and Sāvitrī.
